criteria.title: Positioning an ordinary bed cannot provide
criteria.requirement: The prescriber documents that the member must be positioned with the head raised 35 degrees or more, or in another position an ordinary bed cannot hold.

criteria.title: A diagnosis the positioning need follows from
criteria.requirement: The member has a recorded diagnosis that the prescriber links to the positioning need.

criteria.title: Position changes often enough to need a motor
criteria.requirement: The prescriber's note states that the position must change several times a day or without delay, which a manual crank cannot do.

evidence.text: Condition: I50.22 Chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure. Onset 2021-10-05.

Clinical note (Prescriber visit note):
Chronic systolic heart failure, ejection fraction 25 percent.
Orthopnea: she must sleep with the head raised at 45 degrees to breathe, which pillows cannot
hold. The positioning need follows from her heart failure.
Her son thinks she might need to change position at night now and then, possibly; nobody
has kept track of how often, and she has not said whether a crank would do.

value.rationale: The prescriber's clinical note states, 'she must sleep with the head raised at 45 degrees to breathe, which pillows cannot hold.' This meets the requirement of positioning the head 35 degrees or more in a way an ordinary bed cannot hold.

The member has a diagnosis of 'I50.22 Chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure' and the prescriber explicitly links the positioning need to this diagnosis, stating 'The positioning need follows from her heart failure.'

The prescriber's note states, 'Her son thinks she might need to change position at night now and then, possibly; nobody has kept track of how often, and she has not said whether a crank would do.' This is not a direct statement from the prescriber, is vague about the frequency, and does not confirm that a manual crank would be insufficient.
